propositions: The inbound link differ is add-only by construction and never emits a removal when a link is deleted on the peer
The apply layer silently discards removal records via an `action != 'add'` filter, preventing any removal from reaching the store even if the differ emitted one

Arbitrating between inbound removals and outbound additions requires distinguishing 'a link we never pushed' from 'a link the peer deleted', but managed_refs cannot make this distinction from current-pass state alone

A removal-mirroring feature without history-based arbitration would destroy local data on truncated or failed enrichment reads, violating the fail-safe ADD-only design that currently protects against fetcher defects
The inbound and outbound differs operate on the same pre-pass snapshot then both apply, so suppressing only one direction leaves the pass divergent and churning
The ecosystem does not commonly implement peer-side link deletion propagation; comparable tools either refuse it or gate it behind explicit opt-in configuration
